title: American Community Survey, 1-year estimates
publisher: U.S. Census Bureau
description: Population, jobs by industry, household income, rent, home values and unemployment for the nation, the states and the metro/micro areas published in the ACS 1-year release (roughly 65,000+ people), plus the citizen mix of each metro: workers by occupation (C24010), people by age (B01001, B01002), how workers get to work (C08301), education of adults 25+ (C15003) and place of birth (B05002). Census leaves a few small areas out of some of these tables entirely. (Population growth comes from the Census population estimates instead, which compare every year on the same borders.)

title: American Community Survey, 5-year estimates (counties)
publisher: U.S. Census Bureau
description: County population, income, home value, education, age, poverty, broadband, commuting, birthplace, homeownership, health insurance, veterans (civilians 18+) and members of the armed forces (by where they live), pooled over five years so every county (not just large ones) has an estimate. Only the county rows of each national table file are downloaded.
used_for: County lenses (people, prosperity, knowledge, daily life)
Military layer (veterans and armed forces by county)
Metro GDP (population share of a BEA combined county area split between metros)

title: GDP by county and industry (CAGDP2)
publisher: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis
license: Public domain (U.S. Government work); cite as U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis
description: Gross domestic product in current dollars for every county, state and the nation, by industry. Metro GDP is the sum of the metro's counties. BEA withholds some county-industry values to protect confidential data; those are shown as 'no data', never as zero.
used_for: GDP by industry in city and state panels

title: Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages, annual averages by county
publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics
description: Jobs and wages by county for about 40 industries (manufacturing, autos, chips, finance, research labs, universities, software, ports, film, casinos, hotels, airlines, aerospace, public administration, civilian defense staff, utilities and more), from the annual averages of the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages: a count of the jobs covered by unemployment insurance, by the county where the employer's establishment is. It leaves out the self-employed, most farm workers, railroads and uniformed military. BLS publishes metro areas as totals only from 2025 on, so metro figures add up their member counties. County rows withheld for confidentiality are left out, so such sums are lower bounds.

title: Core Based Statistical Area delineation files (July 2023)
publisher: U.S. Census Bureau / Office of Management and Budget (Bulletin 23-01)
description: The official list of counties that make up each metro and micro area, and of each area's principal cities. Used to place each city at its first principal city and to add up county GDP into metro GDP, and to confirm that the population estimates behind growth use the same county lists.

title: PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, county data
publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Division of Population Health
description: Model-based county estimates of adult health measures from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (mostly 2023 survey data in the 2025 release). They are small-area statistical estimates, not direct counts or a happiness survey; small counties are pulled toward their state and demographic averages. Age-adjusted prevalences are used so places with older or younger populations compare fairly. The 2025 release has no core measures for Kentucky or Pennsylvania, and no social-needs measures (e.g. loneliness) for several states; those stay blank, never imputed.

title: Cartographic Boundary Files (states & counties, 1:20M)
publisher: U.S. Census Bureau
description: Generalized state and county outlines. Used to decide which state and county each hex belongs to.

title: Gazetteer Files (metro areas, counties, places)
publisher: U.S. Census Bureau
description: Names, land areas and coordinates of metro areas, counties and cities. Cities are placed at their principal city.

title: Military and DoD civilian personnel by duty state and service/component
publisher: U.S. Department of Defense, Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC)
description: Quarterly counts of active-duty service members (Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, Space Force, Coast Guard), National Guard and Reserve members, and appropriated-fund DoD civilians, by the state of their assigned unit or duty station. State totals only: DMDC publishes no per-installation or per-county figures. Excludes classified data and most personnel on temporary duty or deployed; civilian counts leave out the Defense Logistics Agency (not submitted).
used_for: Military advisor: troops by state and branch

title: Preliminary Monthly Electric Generator Inventory (EIA-860M)
publisher: U.S. Energy Information Administration
description: Every US generator of 1 MW or more in EIA's 'Operating' sheet, with capacity, fuel, status and coordinates. Generators in service (operating or standby) are summed into power plants using net summer capacity (nameplate where that is blank); units out of service are left out, except that a plant's temporarily idle capacity (status OA) is kept as a separate figure.
used_for: Power-plant resources (nuclear, hydro, wind, solar, coal, gas, geothermal, storage)

title: Historical Detailed Coal Production Data (mine level)
publisher: U.S. Energy Information Administration, with MSHA
description: Annual production, employees and operator of every US coal mine, keyed by MSHA mine ID.

title: Tight Oil and Shale Gas Plays, Lower 48 States
publisher: U.S. Energy Information Administration (U.S. Energy Atlas)
description: Outlines of the major US shale and tight-rock plays (compiled 2015–2021), with basin and lithology. Outlines show where the producing formations lie, not production volumes.

title: ETOPO1 global relief model
publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (via ERDDAP)
description: Land elevation and ocean depth, sampled every ~9 km. Each hex's relief (flat, hills, mountains, peaks) comes from the mean and roughness (standard deviation) of the land samples inside it.

title: FAA passenger boardings and all-cargo data, with NASR airport locations
publisher: Federal Aviation Administration (Office of Airports; NASR airport master via BTS NTAD)
description: Calendar-year passenger boardings (enplanements) at every commercial-service airport, with the previous year's figure and the FAA hub class (large, medium, small, nonhub), plus landed weight of all-cargo aircraft (pounds) at the busiest cargo airports. FAA's tables have no coordinates, so airports are placed by their FAA location id in the NTAD Aviation Facilities layer (certificated airports).
used_for: Airports on the map (runway icons sized by hub class)

title: Freight Analysis Framework (FAF5.7.1, regional database 2018-2024)
publisher: Federal Highway Administration and Bureau of Transportation Statistics (hosted by Oak Ridge National Laboratory)
description: Estimated freight flows between 132 domestic FAF zones (metro areas and the rest of each state), by mode and commodity. Domestic shipments only, newest year in the file, in million current dollars and thousand short tons as FAF publishes them. These are model estimates built on the Commodity Flow Survey, not counts. A flow is assigned to its shipping and receiving zones, so it says nothing about the road it took.
used_for: Trade routes (largest freight flows between metro areas in different states)
Trade partners of a city's zone

title: OpenFEMA Disaster Declarations Summaries (v2)
publisher: Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA)
license: Public data (OpenFEMA terms): cite FEMA as the source; no FEMA endorsement implied. Connecticut crosswalk: U.S. Census Bureau, public domain.
description: Every county named in a presidential major-disaster declaration (DR) since 1 January 2000, with the incident type. Each disaster is counted once per county (FEMA lists New England towns separately under the same county code). Biological declarations (the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic, which named every county) and emergency (EM) and fire-management (FM) declarations are left out. A declaration is an administrative act that unlocks federal aid, not a measure of damage; statewide declarations count for the state only. Connecticut's 8 old counties are mapped to the planning regions that contain any of their towns (Census Bureau crosswalk), so a region counts a disaster if it overlaps a declared county.
used_for: disasters.json (Disasters advisor and City View hazards)

title: Higher Education Research and Development (HERD) Survey, public microdata
publisher: National Science Foundation, National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics (NCSES)
description: Research and development spending reported by each US college and university for one fiscal year: total R&D from all sources and the federally funded part. Totals include medical schools, and some universities report together with their medical centre (e.g. Vanderbilt with VUMC); a few combined reports without an IPEDS ID are matched to their lead campus by hand.
used_for: Wonders: great research universities ranked by R&D spending

title: IPEDS institutional characteristics (HD) and 12-month enrollment (DRVEF12)
publisher: U.S. Department of Education, National Center for Education Statistics (NCES)
description: The directory of every US college and university: name, location (coordinates, county and metro), control, and the 2025 Carnegie research designation (R1 = very high research spending and doctorates), plus 12-month unduplicated headcount enrollment, which also counts online-only students.
used_for: Wonders: research-university positions and R1 status

title: Military Installations, Ranges and Training Areas (MIRTA), FY2025
publisher: U.S. Department of Defense, OASD(EI&E) Defense Installation Spatial Data Infrastructure (DISDI); hosted by Esri's U.S. federal data ArcGIS organisation
license: U.S. Government work (the Esri-hosted copy states CC BY 4.0); DoD gives no warranty and does not list every DoD site
description: DoD's inventory of military installations, ranges and training areas: one point per site and the site boundaries, with reporting component (Army, Navy, Air Force, Marines, their reserves, Army and Air National Guard), operational status and a joint-base flag. Space Force bases are filed under the Air Force; Coast Guard (DHS) sites are not included. MIRTA has no headcount or acreage: areas are computed from the boundaries, and no per-base personnel figure exists in public data.
used_for: Military layer: forts and bases on the map

title: Mines data set (Open Government Data)
publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Mine Safety and Health Administration
description: Every mine MSHA regulates, with current status, operator, primary commodity, reported employees and coordinates. Refreshed daily.

title: Natural Earth 1:50m (countries, lakes, rivers)
publisher: Natural Earth
description: Neighbouring countries (Canada, Mexico, Cuba, the Bahamas; shown fogged), large lakes and major rivers. Files are pinned to the natural-earth-vector release v5.1.2.

title: Natural Earth 1:10m roads and railroads
publisher: Natural Earth
description: Interstates, US highways and major state roads, and main railroads, as 1:10m line work. Shown as map art (roads and rail between hex centres), not as statistics: the road alignment dates from Natural Earth's older releases, carries no traffic or owner data, and the rail layer holds about half of the real US rail network. Files are pinned to the natural-earth-vector release v5.1.2.
used_for: Interstates and major highways on the map

title: National Historic Landmarks (National Register of Historic Places GIS locations)
publisher: U.S. National Park Service, Cultural Resources GIS / National Register of Historic Places
license: Public domain (U.S. Government work); restricted sites are excluded by NPS
description: Locations of National Historic Landmarks, the nationally significant subset of the National Register, with reference number, name, type, city, county, state and certification date. The public GIS copy is incomplete; there is no measure of importance or popularity, so any landmark chosen from it is an editorial pick.
used_for: Wonders: the small curated set of iconic landmarks (positions)

title: National Land Cover Database 2021 (CONUS)
publisher: U.S. Geological Survey / Multi-Resolution Land Characteristics Consortium (MRLC)
license: Public domain (U.S. Government work). Dewitz, J., 2023, NLCD 2021 Products, doi:10.5066/P9JZ7AO3
description: 30 m land cover classes for the lower 48 (2021), resampled by MRLC's web coverage service (nearest neighbour) to a ~2 km grid in NAD83 Conus Albers (EPSG:5070). Each hex's biome (forest, scrub, grassland, farmland, wetland, urban…) and its land-cover shares come from about 400 pixels sampled inside it.

title: U.S. Billion-Dollar Weather and Climate Disasters, 1980–2024
publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI)
license: Public domain (U.S. Government work); cite NOAA NCEI
description: Weather and climate disasters that each cost the U.S. at least $1 billion (CPI-adjusted), 1980–2024, by state and hazard. Final release: NCEI ended the series after 2024. Costs are estimates with wide uncertainty and are given per state; one event usually touches many states, so state figures must not be added up into a national total (the national figures come from the event list).

title: NPS Land Resources Division boundaries (unit centroids and boundaries)
publisher: U.S. National Park Service, Land Resources Division
description: The official outline and centre point of every National Park System unit (national parks, monuments, memorials, recreation areas, seashores, parkways ...), with its four-letter park code and unit type. A live layer: the vintage is its last edit date. Boundaries are simplified by the server to about 500 m, far finer than a map hex.
used_for: Protected land under the largest parks
vintage: NPS Land Resources Division boundaries, edited 2026-11-20

title: NPS Visitor Use Statistics: recreation visits by park unit
publisher: U.S. National Park Service, Visitor Use Statistics Office (IRMA)
description: Monthly recreation visits reported by each National Park System unit, summed over the latest complete calendar year. Units count visits with their own methods (road counters with per-vehicle multipliers, entrance gates, ticket sales), so parkways and urban recreation areas count through-traffic and the National Mall memorials each count the same visitors: visits are only compared within like unit types.
used_for: Wonders: national parks ranked by recreation visits

title: Defense Spending by State (online data workbook)
publisher: U.S. Department of Defense, Office of Local Defense Community Cooperation (OLDCC)
description: DoD spending in each state for one fiscal year: contract obligations (by place of performance), grants, and payroll of civilians, active-duty members and Guard/Reserve, with the total as a share of state GDP and per resident, plus the top 10 counties by contract spending and the top 10 contractors in each state. Contract dollars follow where the work is performed (e.g. Northern Virginia, Huntsville AL, Connecticut shipyards), not where bases are.
used_for: Military advisor: defense dollars by state

title: Population estimates, vintage series (PEP)
publisher: U.S. Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program
description: Annual July 1 population for the nation, every state and every metro/micro area, all years estimated together on today's metro borders (July 2023 delineations). Population growth comes from this series so that every area is compared like for like; the population figures shown in panels are the ACS 1-year totals.

title: Principal Ports of the United States (tonnage)
publisher: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Waterborne Commerce Statistics Center (via BTS National Transportation Atlas Database)
license: Public domain (U.S. Government work; no use restrictions)
description: The 150 principal US ports ranked by total cargo tonnage (short tons), with domestic, foreign, import and export tonnage. Each port is a port statistical area, often miles of waterfront along a river, so its map position is the area's centroid and only approximate for long river ports.
used_for: Ports on the map (harbour icons sized by tonnage)

title: 2020 U.S. Religion Census: county file (RCMSCY20)
publisher: Association of Statisticians of American Religious Bodies (ASARB); distributed by the Association of Religion Data Archives (ARDA)
license: Copyright 2022 ASARB. Used under the ARDA usage agreement, which asks for credit and responsible use; only derived county figures are published here. Credit: the data were downloaded from the Association of Religion Data Archives, www.theARDA.com, and were collected by the Association of Statisticians of American Religious Bodies (Grammich et al. 2023).
description: Congregations and their adherents by county in 2020, as reported by the participating religious bodies. Adherents are counted by congregations (members, their children and regular attenders), where the congregation meets, not by asking residents what they believe; about half of Americans are counted, some groups (notably many historically Black denominations) are under-reported, and a county with a big church can show more adherents than residents. Adherents per 100 residents are computed here as adherents ÷ the census's 2020 population × 100 (the file's own rate columns are not used). Traditions follow ARDA's grouping, with Latter-day Saints split out of 'Other'. Connecticut is not shown: this file uses its 8 old counties, which do not nest in the planning regions the map uses.
